83. config show refuses a key it cannot show (2026-10-27) #

Found while building chapter 82 (its section 2): karvi config show no.such.key prints error: not found and exits 0, as 0.36.0 does. Chapter 28's issue 7 made an unknown key an error: not found block among the others, so that a script could take several places from one load; its exit was never decided. Opened on the operator's word after chapter 82's section 4.

What it gains. A misspelt or unset key no longer reads as success: karvi config show ssh.transprots.alt >/dev/null && echo mapped printed mapped. It waits on nothing. The cost: a site's script that read the error: not found block, or counted on exit 0 beside an unknown key, changes.

Executed. The lab build of 648b3a9 (a-today-lab.sh), with a lab configuration in /dev/shm mapping the slot alt, removed after; the script marks standard output out| and standard error err|:

$ karvi config show no.such.key
  out| key: no.such.key
  out| error: not found
  exit 0

$ karvi --set no.such.key=1 config show display.color
  err| config_unknown_key: unknown configuration key for no.such.key at --set[1]
  exit 2

ssh (a table), ssh.transports.native, and the unset slot ssh.transports.other print the same block, exit 0; with three keys named, display.color no.such.key spool.min-free, the two blocks follow the first key's, exit 0. The loader's check (IsKnownLeaf and the removed-keys table) tells a name that is no key from a key a dynamic table could hold (a transport slot, a platform's field, a macro); a fixed key always has a value, its default.

The gap, agreed. In simple terms: config show refuses a key it cannot show, before printing anything, and a name that is no key as --set refuses it.

  1. config show KEY... checks every name before printing anything; the first it cannot show refuses the view, on standard error, red at a terminal, and nothing goes to standard output.
  2. A name that is no key is refused as --set refuses it, by the loader's own check: config_unknown_key (or config_key_removed, config_key_blank), exit 2.
  3. A key a table could hold that the configuration does not set is the new code config_key_unset, exit 2: ssh.transports.other is not set. ssh.transports.native is one, which is true; setting it is refused at load (chapter 82, gap 1).
  4. The error: not found block goes, and the help and the manual page say what replaces it. Chapter 28's issue 7 otherwise stands.

Not taken: one new code for any name the view does not list (... is not in the configuration), plainer, but a misspelt key would carry another code than --set gives it; an unset key shown as value: null, exit 0, a value the configuration does not hold; the keys before a refused one printed first and the refusal after, as ls does, a refusal after a partial answer.

Found: with keys named, config show --format json KEY prints the text blocks, --format json ignored (the keys imply --explain); built as chapter 84.

Built. In one piece:

  • configload.checkName, the loader's name check (blank, removed, not in the registry), shared by the load's assign and by Explain. Explain returns an error: every name is checked first, and a key with no value is config_key_unset; its error: not found branch is gone.
  • config_key_unset in the error registry, docs/ERROR-CODES.md and the registry artifact's code list regenerated; the registry counter stays 32 (a code does not move it, and this release moves it already).
  • config show reports the refusal through reportError, at the code's exit.
  • The help and karvi-config.1; DESIGN's entry on the view (the rule, its Why, and the alternatives not taken); the CHANGELOG's Unreleased entry.
  • The tests: TestExplainRefusesANameItCannotShow (each kind of name, and the first in the order given), TestExplainSeveralKeys over three keys shown, and TestConfigShowRefusesAKeyItCannotShow (exit 2, the line on standard error, nothing on standard output).

Executed after the build. The lab build of the tree with the change (b-built-lab.sh, the same cases and three more), removed after:

$ karvi config show display.color no.such.key spool.min-free
  err| config_unknown_key: unknown configuration key for no.such.key
  exit 2

$ karvi config show ssh.transports.other
  err| config_key_unset: ssh.transports.other is not set
  exit 2

$ karvi config show sessions.idle-timeout
  err| config_key_removed: removed in v0.14.0; the key was read by nothing and has no replacement; remove it from the configuration for sessions.idle-timeout
  exit 2

$ karvi --set display.color=always config show no.such.key 2>&1 >/dev/null | cat -v   # stderr to a pipe
  err| ^[[1;31mconfig_unknown_key: unknown configuration key for no.such.key^[[0m

ssh and no.such.key are config_unknown_key, ssh.transports.native config_key_unset, and "" config_key_blank, each exit 2; the mapped slot ssh.transports.alt is shown, exit 0.

The full battery on a lab build of the tree with the change (battery.sh, a copy in /var/tmp, TMPDIR=/var/tmp): vet, make generated-clean, go test -count=1 ./... (71 packages), and the 19 suites by run_suites in 242 seconds, each exit 0; none left a /tmp/karvi-<uid>, /var/tmp/karvi-<uid>, /dev/shm/karvi, ~/.local/share/karvi, or karvi process. The first run (battery-1) failed TestHelpMatchesParserTable: the help said "as --set refuses it", and a command's help names only the options its parser takes, --set being global; it now says "as the load refuses it", the suites having passed in 246 seconds.

Closed. The evidence is kept beside the tree (release-design-evidence/config-show-unknown-key-2026-10-27: the two labs' scripts and logs, and the two batteries' logs, battery-1 and the last beside it, with battery.sh).

84. config show refuses --format beside keys (2026-10-27) #

Found while designing chapter 83: with keys named, config show --format json KEY prints the text blocks. Opened on the operator's word after chapter 83.

What it gains. A script that asks for JSON gets JSON or a refusal, never text it cannot parse. It waits on nothing.

Executed. The lab build of e9eac78 (a-today-lab.sh), with a lab configuration in /dev/shm, removed after; every case exit 0:

$ karvi config show --format json display.color
  out| key:        display.color
  out| value:      "never"
  out| source:     /dev/shm/kcj/l/karvi.toml:5
  ...
  exit 0

config show --format json --explain prints the whole text view (1,620 lines), and config show --format toml display.color the same block as above: the keys or --explain choose the text view, and --format, either value, is ignored. Only the full view, no key and no --explain, has a JSON form, the values as an object (232 lines, chapter 47's S2.1).

The gap, agreed. In simple terms: --format encodes the full view alone, and beside keys or --explain it is refused.

  1. --format chooses the encoding of the full view alone: the values as TOML lines or as the JSON object.
  2. With keys named or --explain, the view is text, and a --format given beside it, json or toml, is refused before the configuration loads with the new code config_show_format_conflict, exit 4, as karvi's other *_conflict codes: --format json beside display.color, --format json beside --explain.
  3. The help says so: its synopsis gives the two views on two lines.

Not taken: a JSON form of the keys' view, each key an object (value, source, default, environment, reload, lock, resolved, passed), so a script reads a resolved place without sed, a new contract, its field names and its schema to design, for readers that take two lines with sed; the JSON object narrowed to the keys named, keys then meaning a different view by the format; refusing --format json alone, --format toml being ignored there the same.

Agreed with it: the sensitive mark removed. No configuration key is marked sensitive: configschema.Entry.Sensitive is set on none, so the JSON view's <redacted> branch and Explain's "Sensitive keys are metadata-only" never apply, and every key in the registry artifact carries "sensitive": false. A value nothing uses is removed when found; this piece touches the JSON view, and the artifact's change falls within this release's registry 32.

Built. In one piece:

  • config show refuses --format beside keys or --explain before it loads the configuration (config_show_format_conflict in the error registry), the subject --explain where it is given and the first key otherwise; the format's default is the full view's.
  • Entry.Sensitive removed, with the JSON view's redaction and its sort, the encoder ordering a map's keys; Explain's comment. The registry counter's comment names the mark under 32.
  • Regenerated: schema/config-schema.json (the code, and 178 "sensitive" lines gone), docs/ERROR-CODES.md, and karvi-config.1.
  • The help: the synopsis's two lines and the paragraph; DESIGN's entry on the view (the rule, its Why, and the JSON form not taken); the CHANGELOG's Unreleased entry.
  • The test: TestConfigShowFormatBesideKeys (three refusals at exit 4 with a --set naming no key, which the refusal comes before, and the full view's JSON); configShowSets, the configuration both of the file's tests use.
  • The k03 suite's c22, config sh --format json --explain basedir, exit 0, now expects the refusal, still exercising the abbreviated word, both options, and the key.

Executed after the build. The lab build of the tree with the change (b-built-lab.sh, the same cases and one more), removed after:

$ karvi config show --format json display.color
  err| config_show_format_conflict: --format json beside display.color
  exit 4

$ karvi config show --format json --explain
  err| config_show_format_conflict: --format json beside --explain
  exit 4

$ karvi --set no.such.key=1 config show --format json display.color
  err| config_show_format_conflict: --format json beside display.color
  exit 4

--format toml display.color and --format json --show-sources display.color are refused the same way; config show --format json (the same digest, 232 lines, 8,925 bytes), --format toml, and --explain display.color print as before, exit 0.

The full battery on a lab build of the tree with the change (battery.sh, a copy in /var/tmp, TMPDIR=/var/tmp): vet, make generated-clean, go test -count=1 ./... (71 packages), and the 19 suites by run_suites in 258 seconds, each exit 0; none left a /tmp/karvi-<uid>, /var/tmp/karvi-<uid>, /dev/shm/karvi, ~/.local/share/karvi, or karvi process. The first run (battery-1) failed twice: the k03 suite at c22, above, which a search of the suites for config show had missed under its abbreviation; and TestTreeConverts, DESIGN linking this chapter before the copy held it.
